subject: BrightGrid: telemetry windowing & VAT allocation question
messages:
From: Elena Costa <elena@brightgrid.io>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightGrid Billing <billing@brightgrid.io>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing question — Feb invoice spike

Hi Soojin,

We pulled the Feb invoice and see a large, narrow spike that we didn't expect — ~180k additional tokens billed between 05:00–05:12 UTC on Feb 16 (sample attached). Can you help explain: did Redwood change the telemetry/windowing rule or the attribution window? Our engineering team confirms no large test runs in that window.

Two specific asks:
- A short breakdown (per-minute) of requests attributed to our org for that window, with request ids where possible.
- Confirmation of whether the EU subsidiary VAT reverse-charge should apply here; our billing address and tax ID are on the account, but the invoice lists VAT at 20%.

I attached a CSV (brightgrid_usage_202602.csv) with a subset of request_ids and timestamps. If you need a larger export we can provide it. We are hoping to avoid a formal dispute while we collect evidence, but please let us know how you want to proceed.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Costa
Head of Platform Operations | BrightGrid
elena@brightgrid.io
Attachment: brightgrid_usage_202602.csv (CSV, 46 KB)
From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Costa <elena@brightgrid.io>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:05:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing question — Feb invoice spike

Hi Elena — thanks for the example rows, and sorry for the surprise. We flagged the billing impact and started a parallel investigation (billing + infra). Quick summary & next steps: 

1) Immediate action: I've opened a provisional invoice hold for your account while we validate the windowed attribution. That will prevent automatic collections from proceeding for this invoice cycle.

2) Data request: Can you share the full set of request_ids for 05:00–05:15 UTC (even as a compressed export)? That will let us match request ids to our tokenization logs. If it's easier, we can pull a request-level export for your org — I can trigger that from our side and share a redacted sample.

3) VAT note: We see the VAT line on the invoice. Can you confirm which legal entity should be charged (BrightGrid Inc. in the US vs BrightGrid Ltd in the UK/EU)? If it's the EU entity and you have a reverse-charge certificate, we can reissue the invoice net of VAT, but we need the entity ID to attach to the reissued document.

I am attaching a short token-sample export that includes the token attribution path for the sample timestamps you sent — it's preliminary but should help match the rows. Ben / Hannah: looping in for help with the credit calculation and to confirm the collections hold.

Sooj
Soojin Lee
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_token_sample_export_20260217.jsonl.zip (ZIP, 2.1 MB)

Subject: Fwd: BrightGrid: telemetry windowing & VAT allocation question

Looping in Hannah from finance + our billing operations team notes. Hannah — initial read from infra: it's likely a short-term attribution change caused by a TTL interaction on our KV cache that can double-count tokens for a small segment of requests if a retry arrives within a 12s window. We are already rolling a hotfix to tighten the cache TTL math.

Operationally: recommend offering BrightGrid a one-time pro-rated credit equal to the excess tokens above their 7-day baseline for the same time-of-day window (that avoids reprocessing all their logs and is simpler to reconcile on paper). If infra confirms the cache TTL root cause on the larger export then we can escalate to a retroactive meter correction.

Hannah — can you and billing ops calculate a proposed credit amount if we assume the excess is 180,412 tokens billed at their committed rate of $0.0006/token? Also confirm the invoice hold and whether we should issue a provisional credit note while we finish matching.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Hi Soojin / Ben — thank you for the quick responses and for placing the provisional hold. We pulled the full set of request_ids and attached a gzipped export to our ticket (I'll upload to the Drive link you shared). Two quick notes: 

- We confirm the EU subsidiary (BrightGrid Ltd, VAT GB123456789) should be charged and we have a valid reverse-charge certificate; please reissue net of VAT if possible.
- The BrightGrid engineering team matched five request_ids from your sample to a 2xx response that came from our internal test harness — so we think those are genuine BrightGrid requests. However, a second class of request ids appear to be retries from an upstream proxy that re-submitted the same payload 9s later; that fits your TTL-retry hypothesis.

If your proposal is: provisional credit for the delta (180,412 tokens * committed rate) and then a final reconciliation after you confirm the root cause, that sounds good. Please send the provisional credit note and the reissued invoice for the EU entity. We'll confirm once the final matching completes.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Costa
Head of Platform Operations | BrightGrid
